counted.claim: Card C06220-K1 made 3 online product-C charges totalling $2,166.71 over 1.9 days (3660125, 3660126, 3660127); in its 69 transactions of the 60 days before, that kind made up 0%.
Transaction 3660127 was conducted using device D009721, which was marked as New for the account and operated behind an anonymous proxy (IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS).

Flagged transaction 3660127 is the third transaction in a run of three high-value online product-C transactions totaling $2,166.71 between 2017-01-17 and 2017-01-19 (3660125 for $637.13, 3660126 for $758.80, and 3660127 for $770.78), all using new devices behind anonymous proxies on a card with no prior online product-C baseline.

Three other cards belonging to different customers (C05061-K1, C10553-K1, and C07925-K1) exhibited the exact same signature of 2+ online product-C purchases between $510 and $963 from new devices behind anonymous proxies between 2017-01-12 and 2017-01-17, identifying an active cross-customer syndicate.

Card C06220-K1 has 6 prior closed cases including 5 confirmed fraud outcomes (CC-5379, CC-4224, CC-2807, CC-2539, CC-0626) involving online card-not-present and out-of-region card-present fraud, and only 1 cleared alert (CC-0815).

Device D009721 and region 126 in the 7-day window around transaction 3660127 show zero transactions with model scores over 0.5 and lift of 0.0 versus baseline, reflecting deliberate device and region rotation to evade single-element link analysis.

first.section: Section 3a. A case is not a report
first.text: Section 3a. A case is not a report. Two different things, and the agent produces both. **A case** (`CREATE_CASE`) is the bank's internal record of an investigation. Open one whenever fraud probability reaches 0.30, whenever you request evidence, or whenever a customer disputes a charge. A case can be closed as fraud or as legitimate. It can be updated when new evidence arrives. It should be written into the graph so later investigations can find it: a case that names a merchant or a device becomes evidence for the next analyst. **A suspicious activity report** (`FILE_REPORT`) is a regulatory filing sent outside the bank. File one when fraud is confirmed or strongly suspected **and** at least one of these holds: exposure exceeds $1,000; the activity connects to a shared device profile, a shared region cluster, or another customer's fraud; the pattern is coordinated or undocumented (rule R9). A report always has a case behind it. Most cases never need a report. The report narrative must stand on its own: who, what, when, where, how, and why it is suspicious. Deciding correctly between ""case only"" and ""case plus report"" is part of the next-best-action score.

steps.detail: Investigation of alert HHF-002 on card C06220-K1 identified an undocumented, syndicated card-not-present fraud scheme. Between January 17 and January 19, 2017, the card was subjected to three unauthorized online product-C charges totaling $2,166.71 (transactions 3660125, 3660126, and 3660127). Each transaction utilized a different newly introduced device (D009715, D009718, and D009721) operating behind anonymous proxies, matching identical attack patterns seen on peer cards C05061-K1, C07925-K1, and C10553-K1. The activity was confirmed as fraud with a probability of 0.93, resulting in card blocking, case escalation, regulatory reporting under Policy R9, and monitoring of connected accounts.
